input: Write a due diligence memo on Databricks

team.claim: Founded in 2013 by Berkeley researchers Ali Ghodsi, Andy Konwinski, Ion Stoica, Patrick Wendell, Reynold Xin, Matei Zaharia and Arsalan Tavakoli.
Ali Ghodsi is co-founder and CEO, confirmed in the company financing announcement.
Matei Zaharia is co-founder and CTO and a UC Berkeley associate professor; he started Apache Spark during his Berkeley doctorate. Official biography accessed 2026-11-03.
Dave Conte is listed as CFO as of October 2026 by Contrary Research, a secondary investment-research source; official current-role confirmation remains incomplete.
Conte joined as CFO in October 2019 after serving as CFO at Splunk and Opsware; the appointment announcement also identifies earlier experience at Ernst & Young.
Official biography lists Hatim Shafique as COO; previously COO and SVP of Tech Ops at AppDynamics, with earlier roles at CA Wily. Biography accessed 2026-11-03.
Official biography lists Andy Kofoid as President, Global Field Operations; prior executive roles include Salesforce, ExactTarget and Dassault Systemes. Biography accessed 2026-11-03.

Bloomberg reported AI chief Naveen Rao would leave his operating role to start a computing venture in September 2025; Databricks confirmed a transition to an advisory role and planned investment in his startup.
TechCircle reported India/SAARC VP Anil Bhasin departed on 2025-01-15 to pursue a cybersecurity venture; he previously worked at UiPath, Palo Alto Networks and Cisco.

funding.claim: Latest disclosed round found before 2026-11-03: company announced $5 billion closed at a $190 billion valuation on 2026-08-13, led by Coatue alongside Blackstone, MGX, T. Rowe Price-advised accounts and new investor Sixth Street Growth.

Reuters reported completion of approximately $5 billion equity funding at a $134 billion valuation on 2026-02-09, plus separate $2 billion debt financing led by JPMorgan Chase; this followed the Series L announcement, not a separate additional equity round.
Company announced Series L raising more than $4 billion at a $134 billion valuation on 2025-12-16, led by Insight Partners, Fidelity Management & Research Company and J.P. Morgan Asset Management.
Company announced closing $1 billion Series K at a valuation above $100 billion on 2025-09-08; co-leads were Andreessen Horowitz, Insight Partners, MGX, Thrive Capital and WCM Investment Management.
Reuters reported $10 billion Series J financing at a $62 billion valuation announced 2024-12-17, led by Thrive Capital.

output.verdict: As of 2026-11-03, Databricks looks strong on enterprise adoption, expanding data-and-AI workloads and access to capital, although the latest operating metrics remain company claims. Proceed to deeper diligence rather than an investment conclusion: prioritize audited revenue and margins, cash-flow adjustments, capitalization terms, cloud and model-provider economics, customer cost friction and the unresolved copyright litigation.

business.claim: Company claim: sells a unified enterprise Data + AI Platform spanning data engineering, warehousing, governance, analytics and AI agents; products include Lakeflow, Lakehouse, Unity Catalog, Agent Bricks, Genie and Lakebase.

Company claim: consumption-based pricing includes pay-as-you-go compute and discounted committed-use contracts; DBUs measure processing usage. Storage and networking costs depend on cloud services; Microsoft bills Azure Databricks usage directly.
Company claim as of 2026-08-13: headquartered in San Francisco with more than 30 offices globally and enterprise customers worldwide.

traction.claim: Company claim as of 2026-08-13: more than 20,000 organizations use the platform; named customers include adidas, AT&T, Bayer, Block, Mastercard, Rivian and Unilever.
Company claim as of 2026-08-13: more than 1,000 customers consume above a $1 million annual revenue run-rate and more than 100 above $10 million.

Company claim as of Q2 reported 2026-08-13: revenue grew more than 80% year over year; Lakehouse warehousing exceeded $1.5 billion annual revenue run-rate, growing more than 100%; Lakebase exceeded $100 million run-rate.
Company claim: Microsoft partnership expanded on 2026-07-23 into the 2030s, including Azure infrastructure commitments and integration of Genie and governance into Microsoft products.

Company claim: announced a $100 million multiyear OpenAI partnership on 2025-09-25 to make models natively available through its platform and Agent Bricks; the release also identifies OpenAI as a Databricks user.

red_flags.claim: Valuation underwriting: the $190 billion financing valuation accompanies company-reported annualized revenue and adjusted cash-flow measures rather than audited financial statements; validate revenue quality, cash-flow adjustments and financing preferences before investing.

Training-data copyright exposure remains material to investigate: the DBRX claim survived the April 2026 dismissal motion. Obtain updated docket, training-data provenance, indemnities and potential-loss analysis; liability is not established.
Product adoption and budget friction warrant reference checks: G2 reviews repeatedly flag complexity, learning curve and cost management.
Execution and retention warrant diligence: Glassdoor reports declining aggregate ratings and weaker work-life balance; this is a directional employee-review signal, not proof of employee attrition.
AI leadership continuity warrants review following Naveen Rao’s transition out of his operating role; the reported advisory relationship does not eliminate succession and knowledge-transfer risk.

reputation.claim: Glassdoor aggregator snapshot accessed 2026-11-03: 4.0/5 overall from 1,712 reviews, 77% recommend and 92% CEO approval; the page reports a 3% rating decline over twelve months and 3.3/5 work-life balance. Anonymous self-selection limits representativeness.

G2 review aggregator snapshot accessed 2026-11-03: users praise collaboration, integration and unified workflows; recurring negative themes include learning curve, complexity and cost management. Aggregated review themes are not a representative enterprise-customer survey.

PissedConsumer aggregator displays a 2025-04-17 complaint about a failed certification exam and replacement-voucher support. Its AI summary also alleges billing/pricing and slow-support problems; the evidence is too thin to infer an enterprise-wide complaint rate.

TechTarget critical analysis warned that acquisitions including Mooncake and Neon could create fragmented, difficult-to-integrate infrastructure; this is an analyst risk assessment, not a demonstrated product failure.

missing_fields: Audited financial statements, current recognized annual revenue, gross margin, operating income, net income, balance-sheet cash and cash-flow reconciliation
Current total headcount, verified hiring outcomes, attrition and comprehensive layoff history
Current complete executive roster and primary-source confirmation of CFO currentness
Customer concentration, contract mix, cohort consumption and cloud-provider revenue split
Full historical financing ledger, current cap table, liquidation preferences, dilution and debt covenants
Copyright docket developments after 2026-04-21, class-certification status and quantified legal exposure
Comprehensive regulator-enforcement, sanctions, export-control and beneficial-ownership screening; no clearance conclusion established
Comprehensive breach/incident history after the SOC 3 reporting period and final disposition of the March 2026 security allegation
Representative customer complaint rates, support/outage metrics and independently validated employee-review trend

financial_signals.claim: Company claim as of Q2 reported 2026-08-13: exceeded $7 billion annualized revenue run-rate. This is a run-rate, not reported full-year recognized revenue.
Company claim as of 2026-08-13: positive adjusted free cash flow over the preceding twelve months; the release does not establish GAAP profitability or provide an audited reconciliation.
Company claim for Q3 reported 2025-12-16: $4.8 billion revenue run-rate, more than 55% year-over-year growth and net retention above 140%.
CNBC reported $2.6 billion revenue for the fiscal year ended January 2025; unlike the newer run-rate figures, this is an annual revenue statement, not an independent analyst estimate.

Company claim as of 2025-03-06: approximately 8,000 employees in 23 countries and plans to more than double its San Francisco employee footprint over the next two years; these are a historical baseline and forward plan, not verified current headcount.
Reuters reported a 2025-04-24 company plan to increase India headcount more than 50% to above 750 by fiscal-year end and invest more than $250 million locally; completion is unverified.

legal_and_regulatory.claim: Court order in In Re Mosaic LLM Litigation, N.D. California, 24-cv-01451: on 2026-04-21, Judge Breyer denied dismissal and striking of renewed DBRX copyright allegations against Databricks. Authors sufficiently pleaded a claim; this is not a finding of infringement, damages or class certification.

DOJ/OCAHO order in Ferrero v. Databricks: immigration-related employment-discrimination proceeding was dismissed with prejudice on 2024-09-04 after the parties reported full settlement; the order does not disclose settlement terms or adjudicate liability.

BDO SOC 3 opinion dated 2025-08-15 found effective controls within its security, availability and confidentiality scope for 2024-07-01 through 2025-06-30. Management reported no system incidents causing failure to meet commitments during that period; this is not a comprehensive no-breach assurance.

Cybersecurity News reported a TeamPCP-related compromise allegation on 2026-03-30, but quoted Databricks Security saying its internal investigation found nothing and requested evidence beyond a screenshot. Treat as an unconfirmed allegation, not an established breach.
